src/infrastructure/persistence/in-memory-task-repository.ts: `export class InMemoryTaskRepository implements TaskRepository`; `findByProject(projectId, filter: TaskFilter)` is the only place the task filter rule is applied
src/infrastructure/persistence/in-memory-user-repository.ts: `export class InMemoryUserRepository implements UserRepository` with the same nextId/save/findById shape
All three files define `nextId(): string { return randomUUID(); }`. This is repeated adapter boilerplate, not a duplicated domain invariant
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All three files handle one concern: Map-backed, in-memory adapters for the domain repository ports. Each class implements its domain interface the same way (InMemoryProjectRepository → ProjectRepository, InMemoryTaskRepository → TaskRepository, InMemoryUserRepository → UserRepository). Each keeps a private readonly Map keyed by entity id and exposes the same nextId/save/findById shape. None of them skips the domain abstractions. The task-specific query logic (status and assignee filtering in findByProject) exists only in InMemoryTaskRepository, so that rule lives in one place. The files do repeat boilerplate: nextId() returning randomUUID() and the Map-based save/findById appear in all three. This is structural likeness between parallel adapters for different aggregates, not a business rule or invariant split across files. A shared generic base class could remove it, but the rubric doesn't require that, and the repetition doesn't risk inconsistent behaviour beyond an ID-generation choice. The module is coherent and passes.
